q1_issues.issue: The scale `price` is invented — no word in the clause supplies a dimension noun, and the rule is that an unstated scale takes the reserved symbol `unspecified`, never a world-knowledge dimension.
Same invented `price` scale on the upper bound.

The bounds are asserted at TOP LEVEL of sk_sales_1, so the KB now says sales really were at least $6.9 billion, whereas the sentence says only that Intel predicted it — the predicted content leaks out as fact.

(Ordinal sk_quarter_1 2 year) puts `year` in Ordinal's scale slot, which is specified as the associated event or an explicit -est dimension; the instruction set's own form for a fiscal period with no stated year is the bare constant (`second_quarter`), not a witness plus Ordinal.

"At the end of the second quarter" is encoded as an `end` entity that is PartOf the quarter and then used as a Time filler; Time takes structured calendar terms or bare deictic/named symbols, and PartOf's two jobs are object components and group members, neither of which is a period boundary.
(GroupOf sk_sales_1 sale) types a financial aggregate as a set of individual `sale` members, which the text does not state; the figure is a single mass quantity.

q2_gaps: a monetary magnitude with a scale word ("$6.9 billion") — no licensed magnitude/unit convention, and the parse coined the unit `billion_dollar`
"between X and Y" as a two-sided range on a measure
"at the end of <period>" as a temporal frame — Time takes calendar terms, and `End` is an interval endpoint of an eventuality, not a period-boundary anchor
ordinal position of a calendar period ("the second quarter") — Ordinal's scale slot has no fit, and the bare fiscal-period constant is licensed only for bound Time terms
a non-factive prediction whose content rides an NP object ("predicted sales of $X") — sealing is finite-clause-only, so there is no way to record the content without asserting it
the sequence adverb "initially" — explicitly has no licensed slot (correctly dropped here; registering the gap)
notes: The event skeleton (predict / Agent intel / Past / Theme) is right and the Agent-not-Experiencer choice passes the progressive test; the damage is in the measure slots — an invented scale, a coined unit, and the predicted figures asserted as fact.
